topic: Charles Ponzi: the 1920 Boston scheme that gave 'Ponzi scheme' its name

sentences.text: Charles Ponzi promised fifty percent profit in forty-five days.
To pay everyone, he needed one hundred sixty million coupons, but only twenty-seven thousand existed.
A newspaper questioned him, and he paid a crowd two million dollars in three days.
His bank was seized, and investors lost about twenty million dollars.
He admitted one of eighty-six fraud counts: five years.
He died in Rio with seventy-five dollars.

sentences.editorial: closing question for viewers, not a claim

claims.claim: Charles Ponzi promised clients a 50% profit within 45 days or 100% profit within 90 days.
claims.excerpt: He promised clients a 50% profit within 45 days or 100% profit within 90 days

claims.claim: The scheme claimed to profit by buying discounted postal reply coupons abroad and redeeming them at face value in the U.S.
claims.excerpt: buying discounted postal reply coupons in other countries and redeeming them at face value in the U.S.

claims.claim: Financial journalist Clarence Barron noted that 160 million coupons would have to be in circulation to cover the investments, while only about 27,000 actually were.
claims.excerpt: 160 million postal reply coupons would have to be in circulation. However, only about 27,000 actually were.

claims.claim: On 26 July 1920 the Boston Post began articles asking hard questions; the articles caused a run on the company, and Ponzi paid out $2 million in three days to a crowd outside his office.
claims.excerpt: Ponzi paid out $2 million in three days to a wild crowd outside his office.
claims.context: The Post series began 26 July 1920 (stated in the article).

claims.claim: On 11 August 1920 the Bank Commissioner seized Hanover Trust; the news brought down five other banks, and investors lost about $20 million in 1920 dollars, receiving less than 30 cents on the dollar.
claims.excerpt: They lost about $20 million in 1920 dollars

claims.claim: Ponzi was charged with 86 counts of mail fraud, pleaded guilty on 1 November 1920 to a single count, and was sentenced to five years in federal prison.
claims.excerpt: Ponzi was charged with 86 counts of mail fraud
claims.context: The guilty plea and the sentence are in the same paragraph of the article.

claims.claim: Ponzi was released in 1934 and deported to Italy on 7 October.
claims.excerpt: On 7 October, Ponzi was officially deported.

claims.claim: He died in the charity ward of a hospital in Rio de Janeiro on 18 January 1949, leaving an estate of $75.
claims.excerpt: He left an estate of $75, which was barely enough to bury him.
